strengths: The paper addresses a relevant problem: improving generalization in multi-task vision models. Its modular construction can be incorporated into MGDA, PCGrad, CAGrad, and IMTL, giving the approach useful practical scope.

Tables 1–4 report recurring improvements across classification and dense prediction benchmarks. For example, F-CAGrad improves MultiMNIST average accuracy from 95.01% to 95.95%, reduces CelebA average error from 8.52% to 8.22%, and improves all reported NYUv2 metrics over CAGrad.

The supplementary calibration results provide evidence beyond accuracy: MultiFashion ECE decreases from 0.117 to 0.033 and Brier score from 0.246 to 0.179. Algorithm 1 and Appendix B provide useful implementation details, and the principal methods, architectures, and datasets are attributed.
weaknesses: The central contribution is not isolated experimentally. There is no comparison against SAM/ASAM applied to a scalarized multi-task loss or direct aggregation of per-task SAM gradients, nor an ablation of separately aggregating loss and flatness gradients. For a linear aggregator, the proposed decomposition recombines exactly into aggregated SAM gradients. The experiments therefore demonstrate benefits over conventional training but do not establish the value of the distinctive aggregation procedure.

The theoretical justification has substantive gaps. The vector maximum in Theorems 1 and 4 is ambiguous: componentwise maxima need not correspond to the common shared perturbation asserted in the text. Algorithm 1 instead uses task-specific perturbations, and adding separately aggregated loss and flatness directions does not generally ensure descent for every robust task objective. Appendix A also bounds Gaussian tail contributions using an unstated bounded-loss assumption. These issues prevent the theory from establishing the claimed justification for the update.

The implemented method is insufficiently specified. Appendix B.2 states that experiments use adaptive SAM, whereas Algorithm 1 and the derivation specify ordinary Euclidean SAM. The adaptive update, selected perturbation radii, and validation protocol for the extensive radius search are not provided. The manuscript claims a public implementation but supplies no repository link.

Practical cost and statistical uncertainty are inadequately characterized. Algorithm 1 requires additional evaluations at task-specific perturbed parameters and two aggregation operations, yet no runtime, memory, or compute-matched comparisons are reported. This matters especially for the 40-task CelebA experiment. Tables 2–4 also omit variability estimates, limiting interpretation of smaller differences despite the stated three-seed dense prediction protocol.

The evidence supports average improvements more strongly than coherent improvement of every task. On NYUv2, F-MGDA reduces segmentation mIoU from 30.47 to 26.42, and F-PCGrad worsens several surface-normal metrics; CelebA reports only an aggregate across attributes. The low-resource and noisy-label settings motivating the abstract are not directly evaluated, and parameter-perturbation robustness does not establish robustness to label noise.
